title: Kevin Rideout: US missionary abducted in Niger released | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Kevin Rideout, an American missionary who was held captive in Niger for nine months has been released to US officials, the missionary organization he worked for said Friday.

“We are grateful to confirm that our good friend and brother in Christ, Kevin Rideout, has been released after over nine months in captivity,” SIM International Director Phil Bauman told CNN in a statement.

“Kevin is in good health in the care of US officials,” the statement said, adding that Rideout will soon be reunited with his family.

Rideout was kidnapped from outside of his home in the capital, Niamey, on October 21, 2025, according to SIM, a Charlotte-based Christian missionary organization which says it serves in more than 70 countries.

He was seized by three unidentified men, who later headed toward the western Tillaberi region of Niger, where Islamist militants are active, Reuters news agency reported at the time, citing an unnamed diplomat.

The day after the kidnapping, the US Embassy in Niger warned of a “heightened concern about the threat of kidnapping” and upped its security requirements for Embassy personnel.

A US official told CNN that Rideout is in FBI custody and is doing very well. The New York Times firstreportedhis release.

US President Donald Trump said in a post onTruth Socialthat he helped with the release of Rideout, who he called a “wonderful Christian Missionary.”

“Kevin, the United States of America looks forward to welcoming you HOME. Glad to have helped!” he wrote.

The FBI declined to comment when contacted by CNN.

It was not clear how or when he was released, or which group was holding him at the end of his captivity, the Times reported, adding he may have recently moved.

Niger has faced a surge in attacks from militant groups linked to al Qaeda and the so-called Islamic State, particularly in the tri-border region with Mali and Burkina Faso, and along its southern border with Nigeria.

In May, the US and Nigerian forceskilled senior ISIS commander Abu-Bilal al-Minuki.

CNN has reached out to the White House, the State Department and the Pentagon for comment.

CNN’s Jennifer Hansler contributed to this report.

CNN’s Jennifer Hansler contributed to this report.
